clue.text: The best lubricant for a bed's surface

parts.note: 'the tops' is slang for the very best
oil is a lubricant

explanation.surface: Advice on which oil to use for the surface of a bed, as if furniture care.
explanation.walkthrough: The bed is a garden flower bed, not furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: The uppermost layer of earth is what covers a garden bed, so it is that bed's surface.

clue.text: Skinny French chum must get in substance needed for growth

indicators.note: must get in means the French friend goes inside the skinny word

parts.note: thin means skinny
ami is French for friend

explanation.surface: A thin Frenchman's pal must take a growth supplement.
explanation.definitionFit: Thiamin is vitamin B1, a nutrient essential for growth.

clue.text: Pa's neurotic about preliminary safety procedures

indicators.note: about here means the letters of the phrase are turned around and rearranged

explanation.surface: Dad fussing nervously about safety checks.
explanation.definitionFit: Measures taken in advance to prevent harm are safeguards set up beforehand.

clue.text: Like some fancy stuff old sailors had

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy, sailors
ate means had, as in had dinner

explanation.surface: Old sailors once enjoyed some fancy goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Elaborately decorated things are richly embellished, like fancy stuff.

clue.text: See firm reason for alternative to car?

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning see or look
CO is short for company, a firm
a motive is a reason

explanation.surface: Seeing a company's reason for choosing something instead of a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'car' suggests a motor car, but here it is a railway carriage, which an engine is alternative to on a train.
explanation.definitionFit: On a train the engine is the powered unit, unlike a passenger carriage.

clue.text: Record publicity about coffee

indicators.note: about means the publicity letters go round the coffee

parts.note: PR, public relations, is publicity
a latte is a milky coffee

explanation.surface: A record label's promotional blitz centred on a coffee brand.
explanation.walkthrough: A platter is old slang for a gramophone record.
explanation.definitionFit: Platter is dated slang for a vinyl disc, from its flat dish shape.

clue.text: Get wind up in game

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word for wind is read from the bottom

parts.note: to loop is to wind or coil

explanation.surface: Getting worked up during a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Pool is a cue sport played on a table with pockets.

clue.text: Pointed article about upset in Oxbridge and suchlike

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the whole run of pointed, article and about words is turned upside down

parts.note: aimed means pointed, as with a gun
a is the indefinite article
ca is circa, about

explanation.surface: A pointed piece about a scandal at Oxford and Cambridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' reverses AIMEDACA as a whole. Oxbridge is the joint name for the universities of Oxford and Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: The world of universities and scholarship, of which Oxbridge is the best-known example.

clue.text: Twitch irregularly — or regularly — with this

definitions.text: Twitch irregularly — or regularly — with this

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of the word Twitch is taken

explanation.surface: A spasm that comes now erratically, now steadily.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines it: you twitch irregularly with one. Read as wordplay, 'regularly' takes alternate letters of 'Twitch'; 'irregularly' is a decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: A tic is an involuntary spasm, a nervous muscular jerk.

clue.text: Country-style game introducing meeting

parts.note: RU is rugby union, a game
a rally is a mass meeting

explanation.surface: A rustic sport that kicks off a gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: Done in a rustic way, as in the countryside.

clue.text: Passion of republic once ousting English

indicators.note: ousting means the English letter is thrown out of the republic's name

parts.note: Eire is the former official name of the Irish Republic

explanation.surface: A historical note about passions in a former republic turning against the English.
explanation.definitionFit: Ire is anger, a strong passion.

clue.text: Magician in exhibition centre, one given to exaggeration

parts.note: the NEC is the National Exhibition Centre in Birmingham
a romancer tells exaggerated or fanciful stories

explanation.surface: A conjuror performing at a trade show who embellishes his tales.
explanation.walkthrough: The NEC is a large exhibition venue in Birmingham, England.
explanation.definitionFit: A wizard who works magic by summoning the dead is a magician of a dark kind.

clue.text: Lowly enemy in a period between actions?

parts.note: mean can mean lowly or humble, as in 'of mean birth'
time is called the enemy, as in the phrase 'time is the enemy'

explanation.surface: A humble foe lurking in the pause between two acts of a story.
explanation.definitionFit: The interval while waiting for the next event is the interim, a gap between deeds.

clue.text: Row with almost everyone about old-fashioned system of society

definitions.note: an adjective: relating to the medieval system of lords and vassals

parts.note: a feud is a row or quarrel

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the word for everyone is left off

parts.note: all means everyone

explanation.surface: A quarrel with nearly everybody over an outdated social order.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things relating to the medieval order of lords, vassals and serfs.

clue.text: Number gathered around November — stars and VIPs

indicators.note: gathered around means the number word closes round the November letter

parts.note: a digit is a number
N is November in the NATO alphabet
Aries is a constellation, a group of stars

explanation.surface: A crowd gathered round in November for celebrities and VIPs.
explanation.definitionFit: Officials of high rank are the important people at an event.

clue.text: Our father's working beyond closing time?

indicators.note: working means the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Dad is still at the office long after closing.
explanation.definitionFit: Outside normal business opening, as with a late drink after the pub shuts.

clue.text: Catches in preparation for cricket match

definitions.meaning: ... as a verb means catches, like fish
practice sessions in netted enclosures before a cricket game

explanation.surface: Fielders practising their catching before a cricket game.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, players warm up in nets: practice pitches fenced with netting.
explanation.definitionFit: To snare fish is to trap them, and cricketers' practice takes place in netted lanes.

clue.text: One cast left in hovel with oppressive atmosphere

indicators.note: in means the one, cast and left letters sit inside the hovel

parts.note: a sty is a filthy hovel
I is the Roman numeral one
to fling is to cast or throw

explanation.surface: A lone actor cast away in a stuffy shack.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done stiflingly is done in a smothering, airless way.

clue.text: Two squares have each run up in fancy dress

indicators.note: two means the square number word appears twice
each run up means in each copy the run letter is moved higher, toward the start

parts.note: four is a square number, two squared

explanation.surface: Two people in squares who each run to a fancy-dress party.
explanation.walkthrough: R is the cricket abbreviation for run; in each FOUR it moves up the down entry, giving FROU.
explanation.definitionFit: Frills and ruffles on clothing are fussy ornamentation, the finery of an elaborate gown.

clue.text: Tedious person holding fair opinion in newspaper survey?

indicators.note: holding means the tedious person's letters wrap around the word for fair

parts.note: a bore is a tedious person
OK means fair or middling
a view is an opinion

explanation.surface: A dull columnist sharing a fair-minded view in a newspaper poll.
explanation.definitionFit: A press critique of a new publication surveys a work in print for readers.

clue.text: Knight coming to court drinking hot soup

parts.note: Sir Bors is one of King Arthur's Knights of the Round Table

indicators.note: drinking means the court letters take in the hot letter

explanation.surface: A knight arriving at court and sipping hot soup.
explanation.definitionFit: Borscht is an Eastern European beetroot broth.

clue.text: Phone sound — what you get when engaged?

definitions.meaning: the noise a telephone makes when called
an engagement brings a band for the finger

explanation.surface: A telephone tone and the engaged signal you hear on a busy line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engaged' looks like the busy-line tone, but here it means betrothed.
explanation.definitionFit: A telephone trills when called, and a betrothed person receives a jewelled band.

clue.text: Bit of food and drink — kilo the female's put on must be hidden

indicators.note: must be hidden means those letters go inside the drink

parts.note: gin is a drink

indicators.note: put on in a down clue means the female word sits above the kilo letter

parts.note: her is the female pronoun, with 's read as 'is'
K is kilo in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A snack and a drink, with a woman hiding the weight she has gained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put on' suggests gaining weight, here a kilo, but it places HER above K.
explanation.definitionFit: A small pickled cucumber is a snack-sized morsel of food.

clue.text: Country match starting late by church

indicators.note: starting late means the first letter of the match word is dropped

parts.note: to agree is to match
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A football match kicking off late beside a church.
explanation.definitionFit: Greece is a nation in south-east Europe.

clue.text: Naughty rebel captures queen

indicators.note: captures means the rebel's letters close round the queen's

parts.note: to rise is to rebel, as in rising up

explanation.surface: A rebel seizes the queen in a cheeky coup.
explanation.definitionFit: Risqué material is slightly indecent, so mildly naughty.

clue.text: Perhaps man with heart. as you might say, getting girlfriend?

indicators.note: as you might say means a word sounding like the Latin for heart is used

parts.note: cor is Latin for heart
a date is someone you go out with, a girlfriend

explanation.surface: A man with a big heart, so to speak, landing a girlfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' marks the definition by example: humans are one kind of animal with a spinal cord.
explanation.definitionFit: Humans belong to the phylum of animals with a notochord, so man is one example.

clue.text: Line in earth where river has disappeared

indicators.note: has disappeared means the river letter is removed from the earth word

parts.note: ochre is a kind of earth used as pigment

explanation.surface: A line drawn in the soil where a river has dried up.
explanation.walkthrough: The oche is the line behind which a darts player stands, a pub game staple in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: In darts, the throwing line on the floor is called the oche.

clue.text: Study stretch of land by river — a problem affecting movement here?

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
a tract is a stretch of land
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Studying a stretch of land by a river where something hampers movement.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ure is a river in North Yorkshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical shortening of muscle or tendon that restricts a joint's mobility.

clue.text: Joshua's father's sister

definitions.meaning: in the Bible Joshua is the son of ...
a religious sister in a convent

explanation.surface: A family tree query about a Biblical aunt.
explanation.definitionFit: Joshua is called the son of Nun in the Old Testament, and a convent sister takes vows.

clue.text: Stuck in chair — knitting needle

indicators.note: stuck in means the word sits inside the run of letters chair knitting

explanation.surface: A knitting needle wedged in an armchair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needle' looks like the knitting tool, but it is a verb meaning to annoy.
explanation.definitionFit: To needle someone is to annoy them, a synonym.

clue.text: Feature of monastic life certainly after Mass

indicators.note: after means the certainly word follows the mass word

parts.note: a ton is a unit of mass
sure means certainly

explanation.surface: Monastery life seems assured after attending Mass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass' looks like the church service, but it is a physical quantity measured in tons.
explanation.definitionFit: Monks traditionally shaved the crown of the head, a distinctive part of monastic life.

clue.text: Hat — no as-you-were instructions when it's back to front

indicators.note: back to front means the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
stet is a proofreader's instruction meaning let it stand, so stets are as-you-were instructions

explanation.surface: A proofreader puzzling over a hat with no instructions to restore anything.
explanation.definitionFit: A Stetson is a wide-brimmed cowboy hat.
